speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, please describe the episode where you lost consciousness. Did you witness it, and if so, did you see any shaking, jerking movements, or unusual eye movements?

speaker: Patient
text: 53-year-old male. The patient was brought to the emergency department after an episode of loss of consciousness that occurred 1 hour ago, immediately after micturating. His wife found him unconscious on the bathroom floor. He regained consciousness after about 30 seconds without any confusion or amnesia for the event. No history of urinary incontinence during the event.

speaker: Doctor
text: That loss of consciousness immediately after urination is a critical clue; did you notice any change in heart rate or blood pressure right before passing out, and do you have a history of heart disease or diabetes? REQUEST TEST: ECG, Blood_Glucose, Electrolytes.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: ECG: No abnormalities, Blood_Glucose: Within normal limits, Electrolytes: Within normal limits

speaker: Patient
text:
My main symptom is Episode of loss of consciousness. I also have Regained consciousness quickly without confusion, No urinary incontinence, No bite marks or injuries.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Commotio Cordis (Neurogenic Stimulation of the Vagus Nerve during Micturition)
